readback.description:
MECHANICAL worktree ban (punchlist F4/F5; owner standing order: worktrees must never come back). Pre-designed recipe applied exactly from docs/worktree-ban-handoff.md (jain-split root):

1. verify-worktrees enforcement: verify_managed_worktree counts linked worktrees via the existing strict_git_output(worktree list --porcelain) and fails when more than the primary checkout exists. Unit test added: repo with a linked worktree yields status==fail; removal restores pass.
2. hooks/pre-push (exact handoff body): refuses push when extra worktrees exist. Rollout wired as splitctl jeryu-doctor --install-hooks (sets core.hooksPath per managed repo to the shared hooks dir), added to just jeryu-ready-apply. No repo currently sets core.hooksPath and no repo has active .git/hooks, so the rollout is non-disruptive.

Verification (sandbox clone at 88a673c6 + this diff): cargo build green; cargo test --locked 27/27 green incl. the 2 worktree tests; hook drill: push refused with 1 extra worktree (exit 1, lists worktrees), allowed after removal; just fast green. just required is red at validate-manifest --check-derived on unmodified main too (fleet derived manifests embed canonical sha d726e7b4 which matches no committed manifest; the v8.0.1 manifest-pin lane is actively resyncing, /home/ubuntu/jain-split/jain/repos.manifest.toml last modified 12:36Z) — pre-existing cross-lane skew, not introduced by this diff.

NOT included: registering verify-worktrees as a required protected-main check. splitctl protection-apply PUTs immutable_main_policy(required_check) whose required_status_checks is exactly [required_check] — registering verify-worktrees that way would REPLACE each repo required check instead of adding one. Staged for owner/Codex with a policy change that adds, not replaces.

Review note (honest): this is a mechanical application of the pre-designed handoff recipe; the review below is the same lane confirming exact-recipe conformance, not an independent second design review.
